| **Author** | Imas, Koh & Legg (Google DeepMind) |
| **Published** | 2026-10-31 |
| **Type** | framework — Imas, Koh & Legg — Four Regimes of AGI |
| **Source** | <https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05417> |
| **Tags** | Mild REP (wages, not jobs), DIFF |
| **Policy stance** | off |
| **Likelihood** | probable — Today's AI already matches professionals on many bounded tasks while coordinating poorly (team scaling exponent 0.48–0.68), and softer entry-level hiring with a 4.2% fall in starting wages fits wages moving before organisations do. |
| **Assessed** | 2026-11-27 |

AI matches capable humans on individual tasks but cannot coordinate at scale, so firms and headcounts barely change and markets stay split among many small and medium firms. AI firms enter niche markets and cut prices, and wages fall before jobs are lost.

## Social contract scores (draft)

| Promise | Score | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hard work pays | 2 | Nobody loses a job, but workers whose skills AI matches see pay pulled toward the cost of compute; in the example specialist wages fall from 4.15 to 2.90 and coordinator wages from 2.41 to 1.30. |
| Affordable essentials |  | Not addressed: AI lowers goods prices in niche markets, but the extract says nothing on housing, food, energy or care. |
| Reliable safety net | 3 | The model has no transfers, but headcounts stay intact and unemployment is zero, so the safety net is not stretched. |
| Responsive government |  | Not addressed: the model has no government and the authors recommend only measurement. |
| Time for what matters |  | Not addressed: nothing on hours, family or community. |
